questions.q: What is a 'circular definition,' per this lesson?
options: A definition that restates the term using itself or a close synonym, like 'Active: a customer who is active'
A definition that includes a diagram
A definition with more than one sentence
A definition that has been reviewed by multiple stewards
questions.explain: A circular definition only makes sense to someone who already understands the term — it fails exactly the people a glossary is meant to help.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four parts of this lesson's definition quality test?
options: Specific
Self-contained
Measurable where possible
Written by a certified data scientist
questions.explain: The four tests are specific, self-contained, measurable where possible, and free of implementation detail — who wrote it isn't one of the quality criteria.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say 'Active Customer: WHERE LastPurchaseDate >= DATEADD(day, -90, GETDATE())' is a weak glossary definition?
options: It's implementation leakage — a query, not a business definition, and it breaks if the underlying table changes
It is too long to fit in a glossary tool
It uses incorrect SQL syntax
It doesn't mention the word 'customer'
questions.explain: This belongs in the data dictionary (Chapter 3), not the glossary — a business definition should state the rule in plain language, not the exact query that implements it today.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a 'vague qualifier' this lesson warns against?
options: "at least one completed purchase in the trailing 90 days"
"recently" or "significant"
"owned by the Finance data domain"
"DECIMAL(18,2)"
questions.explain: Words like 'recently' or 'significant' hide an undefined threshold behind language that sounds precise but isn't — the lesson says to state the actual number if one exists.

questions.q: In the worked rewrite, what made the 'better' version of the Active Customer definition pass all four tests?
options: It stated a specific, measurable threshold (90 days) without naming any column or query
It was shorter than the weak version
It included the exact SQL query used to calculate it
It avoided mentioning any numbers at all
questions.explain: 'At least one completed purchase in the trailing 90 days, measured from the nightly refresh' is specific, measurable, self-contained, and free of implementation detail — all four tests at once.
